I merged https://github.com/scolladon/craft/pull/67 as `6114371`. The test fixtures no longer use your global gpg signing, so they pass whether or not signing works. CI passed and `bash scripts/ci.sh` passes.

**Root cause:** the fixture commits used your global `commit.gpgsign=true`. To prove it without needing machine load, I pointed git at a global config whose signer always fails (`gpg.program=false`):
- `run-ledger.test.js`: 71 of 73 failed.
- `worktree.test.js`: 9 of 9 failed.
- `hooks.test.js`: 35 failed. It wasn't in the backlog entry, but it builds repos with the same helper (`test/helpers/craft-run.js`), so the fix covers it.
- No other suite was affected.

**Fix (test files only):**
- **Signing off:** both fixture git wrappers now pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`, taken from a new `test/helpers/commit-signing.js`. This flag overrides every git config file.
- **Regression tests:** one each for `createRunRepo` and `mkWorktreeNoRemote` under the failing signer, plus a test that the failing signer really breaks a normal commit. With the flag removed, the fixture tests fail with `gpg failed to sign the data`. With it, all five affected suites pass (164/164) with both your normal config and the failing one.
- **Review fixes:**
  - When `createRunRepo` fails, it now deletes its temp dir before rethrowing; before, a failed run left a `craft-run-*` folder behind.
  - The new worktree test now uses the same setup and teardown helpers as the rest of the file.
